_about: Science layer per object class (contract I4, WORKSPLIT C3). Built by data/scripts/build_classes.py: edit there, not here. Each number is {value, source, checked}. checked: 'read' = read on the source page 14 Nov 2026; 'search' = quoted from that source in a web search, page not opened; 'calculated'; 'team' = our working threshold, not a literature value. Class entries sit at the top level under the ids in class_ids.

brown_dwarf_d6_over_d4.note: Brightness at 4.7 um over brightness at 3.1 um. A plain star falls to ~0.44 here (calculated: Rayleigh-Jeans tail, (3.12/4.71)^2); methane at 3.3 um makes T and Y dwarfs much brighter at 4.7 um. Separates eps Indi B and WISE 0855 from every field star in our 5 reports. Not a published limit.

mira_min_ratio.note: Factor between brightest and faintest visit above which a variable is drawn as a Mira. 2.5 = 1 magnitude. Our R Dra shows a factor ~17 (halo light, core saturated); RW Aur 1.9. Caution: published K-band amplitudes of Miras are 0.3-0.8 mag (factor 1.3-2.1, source mira_kamp), so a quiet Mira can fall below this and be drawn as a young star. The GCVS definition (2.5-11 mag) is for visible light, not infrared.

red_dwarf_min_bp_rp.note: Gaia colour BP-RP. Table: M0V = 1.84, M2V = 2.23, so 2.0 means 'about M1 or later'.

variable_min_ratio.note: Smallest brightest/faintest ratio we call variable (with the chi-square test). Chosen above our photometry scatter; not a literature value.

red-dwarf.plain: A small, cool star, the most common kind in the Milky Way. Faint in visible light, easy to see in infrared.

gaia_bp_rp_min.note: Gaia colour BP-RP. Table: M0V = 1.84, M2V = 2.23, so 2.0 means 'about M1 or later'.

rules.spectrum: Brightest near 1-2 um, then falls steadily to 5 um (no rise at the red end).
rules.motion: Nearby ones move measurably: Barnard's Star 10.39 arcsec/yr (data/science-notes.md).

temp_K.note: M4V, the type of Barnard's Star

brown-dwarf.plain: A failed star: too small to shine like the Sun, glowing faintly in infrared as it cools.

d6_over_d4_min.note: Brightness at 4.7 um over brightness at 3.1 um. A plain star falls to ~0.44 here (calculated: Rayleigh-Jeans tail, (3.12/4.71)^2); methane at 3.3 um makes T and Y dwarfs much brighter at 4.7 um. Separates eps Indi B and WISE 0855 from every field star in our 5 reports. Not a published limit.

dip_um.note: Methane bands of T dwarfs (windows in data/bands.json). The 3.3 um band is the deepest.

rise_um.note: Cold brown dwarfs are brightest at 4-5 um; WISE 0855 was found in the WISE 4.6 um band and we see it only above ~3.8 um.

rules.motion: The ones SPHEREx can see are close, so they move: our two are 4.7 and ~8.1 arcsec/yr (data/science-notes.md).

temp_K.note: Upper end: L0 = 2270 K (mamajek). Lower end: WISE 0855, the coldest known, 225-260 K (luhman2014). Y dwarfs are below 500 K (ydwarfs2026).

radius_rjup.note: 'Very close to 1 Jupiter radius'. Mamajek's table gives 0.091-0.104 Rsun for L5 to Y0 = 0.9-1.0 Rjup (calculated, 1 Rjup = 0.1028 Rsun).

mass_mjup_examples.note: eps Indi Bb and Ba, measured from their orbit. The usual 13-80 Jupiter-mass range for the class was not re-checked: do not quote it yet.

temp_K.note: Mid T dwarf, between eps Indi Bb (880-940 K) and Ba (1300-1340 K).

appearance.note: Below ~700 K the true colour is black to the eye: lib3d draws it warmer so it is visible and must label that.

mira.plain: A swollen, dying red giant that pulses: it brightens and fades over months, over and over.

variable_ratio_min.note: Factor between brightest and faintest visit above which a variable is drawn as a Mira. 2.5 = 1 magnitude. Our R Dra shows a factor ~17 (halo light, core saturated); RW Aur 1.9. Caution: published K-band amplitudes of Miras are 0.3-0.8 mag (factor 1.3-2.1, source mira_kamp), so a quiet Mira can fall below this and be drawn as a young star. The GCVS definition (2.5-11 mag) is for visible light, not infrared.

temp_K.note: Models 2750-2860 K (mira_models); R Aql measured 3072 +/- 161 K (mira_iota). The temperature changes through the cycle.

radius_rsun.note: Rosseland radius; R Aql measured 250 Rsun (mira_iota). The radius depends on the wavelength it is measured at.

young-star.plain: A newborn star, a few million years old, still wrapped in the disk of gas and dust it formed from.

variable_ratio_max.note: Factor between brightest and faintest visit above which a variable is drawn as a Mira. 2.5 = 1 magnitude. Our R Dra shows a factor ~17 (halo light, core saturated); RW Aur 1.9. Caution: published K-band amplitudes of Miras are 0.3-0.8 mag (factor 1.3-2.1, source mira_kamp), so a quiet Mira can fall below this and be drawn as a young star. The GCVS definition (2.5-11 mag) is for visible light, not infrared.

variability.value: irregular; dust from the disk can dim it by ~2 mag for months to years

rules.spectrum: Extra infrared light from the warm disk: flatter from 2 to 5 um than a bare star of the same temperature.
rules.motion: None: the nearest star-forming regions are ~140 pc away (data/science-notes.md).

temp_K.note: Spectral types K0 to M6 (ttauri) on the dwarf temperature scale: K0V = 5270 K, M6V = 2810 K. Young stars of the same type can differ by ~100-200 K.
K5V, mid-range. RW Aur's own temperature is not in our notes yet.

star.plain: An ordinary star far in the background. It stays put and keeps its brightness.

d6_over_d4_typical.note: Rayleigh-Jeans tail between the centres of D4 (3.12 um) and D6 (4.71 um): (3.12/4.71)^2.

rules.motion: Not significant over the SPHEREx baseline.

temp_K.note: M0V to G2V (the Sun's type): what dominates a SPHEREx field. Hotter stars exist but are rare.

asteroid.plain: A rock orbiting the Sun. It crosses the patch so fast that it shows up in one visit and is gone in the next.

seen_in_visits.note: Our rule: a source seen once, at the place and date where SkyBoT puts a known asteroid.

spectrum.value: At 3.4 and 4.6 um its light is a mix of reflected sunlight and its own heat

rules.motion: Too fast to link between visits 6 months apart. Speed on the sky and surface temperature were not re-checked: no numbers yet.

comet.plain: A dirty snowball from the outer Solar System. Near the Sun its ices turn to gas and form a fuzzy cloud, the coma.

emission_um.note: Water, carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide gas. In 3I/ATLAS SPHEREx saw CO2 at 4.26 um and no H2O or CO gas.

extended.value: wider than a star: the CO2 coma of 3I/ATLAS reached at least 30 SPHEREx pixels (~348,000 km)

rules.motion: Moves between exposures, like an asteroid.

comet.note: No comet is among our 5 targets and the classifier has no comet rule yet: this entry is for the 3D library and the text.

temp_K.note: +/- 102 K; another published value is 3223 +/- 17 K
true colour is black to the eye

rw-aurigae.note: no checked temperature yet: keep 'assumed' in appearance.json

period_days.note: 245-246 d in secondary lists; confirm in AAVSO VSX (open item in data/science-notes.md)

mamajek.cite: E. Mamajek, 'A Modern Mean Dwarf Stellar Color and Effective Temperature Sequence', version 2022.04.16 (extends Pecaut & Mamajek 2013, ApJS 208, 9)

dawson2004.cite: Dawson & De Robertis 2004, 'Barnard's Star and the M Dwarf Temperature Scale' (Teff 3134 +/- 102 K, R 0.200 +/- 0.008 Rsun), as quoted on Wikipedia

luhman2014.cite: Luhman 2014, discovery of WISE J085510.83-071442.5 (Teff 225-260 K)

ydwarfs2026.cite: 'The Coldest Known Y Dwarfs: Estimates of their Effective Temperatures' (Y dwarfs: Teff < 500 K)

kirkpatrick2021.cite: Kirkpatrick et al. 2021, 20-pc census of 525 L, T and Y dwarfs (old brown dwarfs have radii very close to 1 Jupiter radius)

king2010.cite: King et al. 2010, A&A 510, A99, 'eps Indi Ba, Bb: a detailed study of the nearest known brown dwarfs' (Teff 1300-1340 K and 880-940 K)

chen2022.cite: 'Precise Dynamical Masses of Epsilon Indi Ba and Bb' (2022): dynamical masses of eps Indi Ba and Bb (66.92 +/- 0.36 and 53.25 +/- 0.29 Jupiter masses)

gcvs.cite: General Catalogue of Variable Stars, type M (Mira): V amplitude 2.5-11 mag, period 80-1000 d

mira_models.cite: 'Dynamical Opacity-Sampling Models of Mira Variables. II' (model series: Rosseland radius 241-260 Rsun, Teff 2750-2860 K). Which of the Mira model papers the search quoted is not certain: open it before citing in the submission

mira_iota.cite: IOTA/FLUOR interferometry of Mira stars (R Aql: Teff 3072 +/- 161 K, Rosseland radius 250 Rsun)

mira_kamp.cite: Spectro-interferometric study of Miras: near-infrared K amplitudes typically 0.3-0.8 mag, bolometric 0.5-1.2 mag. Which paper the search quoted is not certain: open it before citing in the submission

ttauri.cite: T Tauri stars: ages < 10 Myr, masses < 2 Msun; spectral types K0-M6 (Barrado y Navascues & Martin 2003; LAMOST DR6 study)

rwaur.cite: 'Recurring Occultations of RW Aurigae by Coagulated Dust in the Tidally Disrupted Circumstellar Disk' (dimmings of ~2 mag in 2010-11 and > 2 mag in 2014-16)

neowise_thermal.cite: 'Asteroid thermal modeling in the presence of reflected sunlight with an application to WISE/NEOWISE observational data': at 3.4 and 4.6 um asteroid fluxes mix reflected sunlight and thermal emission

atlas3i.cite: 'SPHEREx Discovery of Strong Water Ice Absorption and an Extended Carbon Dioxide Coma in 3I/ATLAS' (2025 (CO2 gas at 4.26 um, coma >= 30 px ~ 348,000 km; gas windows 3.0 / 4.26 / 4.7 um)

reports.cite: Our own runs on the 5 targets, 14 Nov 2026
